newsitem.title: FINLAND: Baltic Ice - Ridged ice forming in Bay of Finland.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Ice - Ridged ice forming in Bay of Finland.

text.p: No new waters froze but wind pressed ice in the eastern Gulf of Finland to thicker ridged and rafted form, the Finnish Insitute of Marine Research said on Thursday.
It gave no new restrictions but repeated that only ships with ice-classes I and II with deadweights over 1,300 tonnes would be assisted to Inkoo, Kantvik, Helsinki and Porvoo from February 28.
The restriction for Loviisa, Kotka and Hamina would also be lifted to ice-classes IA and IB with 1,300 deadweight tonnes, or IC and II with 2,000 deadweight tonnes on February 28, it said.

Four icebreakers were on station near St Petersburg and Vyborg in the eastern Gulf of Finland, one near Porvoo and Loviisa, five in the northern end of the Gulf of Bothnia, two in the middle, and one outside Rauma.
One ice-breaker remained on station in the Gulf of Riga.

NOTES: New ice - forming, thin and still moving. Fast ice - not moving level flat ice. Level ice - thick flat ice. Consolidated/compact - compact close ice. Windrow ice - reshaped by wind, thickness varies sharply. Rafted - ridges forming, 10-20 cm thick. Ridged - ridged or hummocked ice. Open - floes with water at rate of 4-6:10. Close ice - floes tightly packed.
